children: Delhivery EV fleet expansion will add up to 2,000 electric commercial vehicles through partnerships with Tata Motors, Euler Motors and Montra Electric

Delhivery has partnered with Tata Motors, Euler Motors and Montra Electric to deploy 1,500–2,000 electric commercial vehicles across its intra-city logistics network over the next 12–18 months, as the logistics company accelerates fleet electrification. The company signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with the three manufacturers on November 13, 2026, with the rollout beginning in Delhi-NCR. The deployment is part of Delhivery’s plan to operate close to 5,000 electric commercial vehicles within three years.
Delhivery Targets Full Intra-City Fleet Electrification

The initiative focuses on vehicles travelling less than 200 km daily, a segment where electric vehicles are increasingly competitive with diesel on total cost of ownership. Electric vehicles currently account for around 12–13 per cent of Delhivery’s eligible intra-city fleet. The company aims to increase the share beyond 50 per cent over the next two to three years and fully electrify its sub-200 km fleet within four to five years.

The transition will cover multiple commercial vehicle categories, beginning with urban delivery vehicles before expanding to higher-capacity models for heavier payloads. Delhivery is also investing in vendor advance payments, charging and parking infrastructure to support adoption.
Charging Infrastructure to Support EV Adoption

The company is piloting charging facilities at its locations, beginning with Delhi-NCR, and plans to provide low-cost charging and free parking for vendor partners. The deployment will include Tata Motors’ Intra EV, Euler Motors’ Turbo City Plus and Montra Electric’s EVIATOR. Euler’s Turbo City Plus will be deployed first for smaller commercial applications, while larger electric vehicles will be introduced subsequently.

Delhivery said the initiative would reduce the environmental impact of logistics operations while maintaining network efficiency and reliability. “Scaling fleet electrification means finding solutions that work across the diverse needs of our network without compromising operational efficiency,” said Prashant Gazipur, Chief Operating Officer, In City Operations, Delhivery.
